title: A20 oxygen and dual tracers permit an unchanged oxygen-use law in a renewal box at 5% tolerance
abstract: We tested whether the 2012-2021 A20 oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 requires a change in oxygen use when age spectra must evolve through aging and surface renewal. A linear program couples initial water, retained water and incoming young water. Scaling the mass measures by the common oxygen-use parameter keeps the full fit linear. At 5% relative CFC-12 and SF6 tolerance and a 50-year age limit, one unchanged saturating oxygen-use law fits both cruise levels in all six paired latitude bins. An explicit fit retains half of the initial water with age-independent removal, uses only water formed at or after the first cruise, and keeps at least 150.237 umol/kg oxygen in each component. Its rate-decay time is five years. The endpoint fit has a constant-volume renewal-box realization with time-dependent exchange. A common constant-rate law leaves a minimum AOU error of 2.749 umol/kg under young input. Tighter 2% tracer tolerance rejects the tested A20 local-renewal laws. Thus a free change in age spectrum is not necessary for the earlier unchanged-law counterexample. The result is conditional compatibility, not attribution. Unknown source saturation, flexible renewal timing, the age limit, sparse cruises and unmeasured source oxygen prevent an estimate of the ventilation share. Code, aggregate results, grid checks and an independent audit are included; external records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Minimum oxygen mismatch with independent endpoints or with aging and young input. The 5% tolerance is a sensitivity box.
Common retained-fraction tests with age-independent removal. Positive fits are valid over continuous ages; the scan does not exclude untested fractions.
